lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: interpreting model parameters in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 5, 10, 20, 40. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Quadratic; the second differences are constant.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 2.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 2.

items.prompt: A population of 400 grows by 10% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 6 years, to the nearest whole number.
Quantity A grows by 61 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: A stays ahead permanently because 61 is larger than 3.
B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 2000(0.86)^t, with t in years. What does 2000 represent?
choices: the total value lost over the asset's life
the number of years until the asset is worthless
the value of the asset when it was new, $2000
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.86, meaning a 14% annual loss

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (1, -7) and (6, -52). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 20, 100, 500, 2500. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
